parsed.rationale: All eleven members are unnamed `extension` declarations on `EnvironmentValues` spread across five distinct packages (`AppServices`, `Playback`, `WXUI`, `Wallpaper`, `PlayerHeaderView`). The name-collision signal fires purely because Swift's `EnvironmentValues` extension pattern requires every module that injects a custom environment key to declare its own `extension EnvironmentValues` block — this is the canonical, idiomatic SwiftUI pattern and the coincidence is entirely structural. No fields or signatures are reported (`fields_or_signature: []` on every record), so there is no shared logic to extract. Consolidating these extensions across package boundaries would introduce artificial inter-package dependencies (e.g., `AppServices` depending on `Wallpaper`) with no benefit. None of the restraint markers are set, but the reason for no-action is that the shared shape encodes unrelated domain concepts whose coincidence is structural only.
